page: Microsoft Azure D32as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dasv7 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing placing the instance in the top 10% tier. Multi-core performance under stress-ng falls within the average range. The server demonstrates strong capabilities in data compression and cryptography, scoring in the top 25% for Passmark CPU encryption and gzip compression, and the top 10% for single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory performance is robust, with a Passmark memory score in the top 25%, though uncached large-block read and write bandwidths remain average.

For specialized tasks, the D32as_v7 shows strong performance in small-model LLM inference, achieving top 10% text generation speeds for 135M parameter models, though performance drops to average or poor as model sizes scale up to 70B parameters. Given its balanced resource density and high single-core clock speed, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for general-purpose workloads, web serving, database operations, and moderate computational tasks that benefit from high-frequency AMD EPYC cores without requiring dedicated local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
